question.problem:
$$ \{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=3{x}_{1}(t)-{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-3{x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}] $$ Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a transformed system with the solution $$ {X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}=\frac{1}{2s}+\frac{7}{2(s-4)},\,{X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}=\frac{3}{2s}-\frac{7}{2(s-4)}. $$ Find the solution to the original initial value problem.
$x(t)=\,\,$ {{field-1}} $\,\,+\,\,$ {{field-2}} $\,\,{e}^{4t}$
{{field-3}} {{field-4}}
question.worked_solution:
To find ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ satisfying the original initial value problem, we apply the inverse Laplace transform to ${X}_{1}(s)$ and ${X}_{2}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{1}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{2s}+\frac{7}{2(s-4)}\} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s}\}+\frac{7}{2}{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-4}\} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1+\frac{7}{2}{e}^{4\cdot t} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+\frac{7}{2}{e}^{4t} \\ {x}_{2}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{2}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{3}{2s}-\frac{7}{2(s-4)}\} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s}\}-\frac{7}{2}{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-4}\} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot 1-\frac{7}{2}{e}^{4\cdot t} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}-\frac{7}{2}{e}^{4t}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
x(t)=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}+\frac{7}{2}{e}^{4t} \\ \frac{3}{2}-\frac{7}{2}{e}^{4t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{2} \\ -\frac{7}{2}\end{aligned}]{e}^{4t}.
$$
